result.title: Finite-Sample Sensitivity of Kernel Metrics for Generative Evaluation
result.summary: Kernel distances such as the Kernel Inception Distance (KID) and the Kernel Audio Distance (KAD) compare generated and reference samples in an embedding space, and model comparisons rest on their values. Each ships with one fixed kernel, and a reported value does not say which changes that kernel detects at the sample size used. We run each default as a permutation two-sample test on real embeddings of symbolic music, audio and images, comparing a sample with an independent sample changed by a mean shift, an isotropic contraction, or a rotation that keeps the mean and the covariance trace and is matched to the shift in transport distance. At 780 samples per side, both defaults rarely detect the rotations in five evaluation spaces, while they detect the shifts in every run. The median-bandwidth Gaussian kernel of KAD detects the contraction and regains power against rotations on image embeddings with an order of magnitude more samples. The cubic kernel of KID contains second- and third-moment information but misses the contraction in most runs, and our experiments do not establish a high-power rotation regime for it over the tested sample sizes. Narrower Gaussian bandwidths restore sensitivity in music and audio, an $\ell_1$ Laplace kernel does so for images, and aggregated tests combine both at nominal level. We recommend that a reported kernel distance state its sample budget and the changes its configuration detects at that budget.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 KID、KAD 的默认核当作置换双样本检验，在符号音乐、音频和图像的真实嵌入上比较固定样本量下对均值平移、各向同性收缩以及与平移在传输距离上匹配的旋转的检测能力，并考察不同带宽、Laplace 核与聚合检验能否恢复敏感性。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究的是生成评价核度量的有限样本功效而非推理机制，但可为比较不同深度、位置或架构的 latent 状态差异时「核距离能否检出旋转、收缩类变化及样本预算如何影响结论」提供可供核查的方法线索。
